messages.content: You are a senior software engineer performing a structured code review of Java source code.

message.content:
Summary
- Overall the file is short and mostly clear. It mixes responsibilities (validation, normalization, resolution, reading) in one static method, uses Spring StringUtils unnecessarily, and lacks defensive checks and documentation. There are a few portability and Java-version issues and a missing private constructor for a utility class.

Detailed review by category

1) Naming
- FileUtils (class): OK for a simple utility class, but it’s a very generic name and can collide with common libraries (e.g., Apache Commons). Consider a more specific name if this is project-scoped (e.g., ProjectFileResolver).
- readFile (method): Name is misleading because the method does more than just read a file — it also tries multiple candidate locations. Consider readFileFromProjectPaths or readAsString (if you keep it generic).
- Parameter name path: acceptable but a bit ambiguous (is it a classpath-style path, absolute, relative?). Consider pathOrResource or pathCandidate.
- Local variables:
  - cwd is fine.
  - trimmed is fine.
  - resolved could be found or resolvedPath (slightly more descriptive).
- Suggestion: Prefer explicit, descriptive names when a method has specific behavior (e.g., readProjectFileAsString).

2) Code structure
- Single-responsibility: The readFile method performs multiple duties: validation, normalization, candidate list construction, file lookup, and reading. This should be split into smaller methods:
  - validateInput(String)
  - normalizeInput(String)
  - buildCandidates(String)
  - findExistingFile(Path[])
  - readFileContent(Path)
- This improves testability and readability.
- Long methods: The method is short but conceptually doing several things; split as above.

3) Best practices
- Missing private constructor for utility class: Add a private constructor to prevent instantiation.
  - e.g., private FileUtils() { throw new AssertionError("No instances"); }
- Unnecessary Spring dependency: org.springframework.util.StringUtils.hasText is used for a simple blank check. Prefer standard library:
  - In Java 11+, String.isBlank() or use trim().isEmpty() depending on semantics. That removes Spring dependency from this utility.
- Path handling & platform portability:
  - The code removes only a single leading forward slash (trimmed.startsWith("/")), which:
    - may not cover Windows backslash root (\).
    - removes only one leading slash (what about multiple leading slashes?), and it treats an absolute Unix path as a classpath-relative path — this should be explicit and documented.
  - Consider normalizing leading separators more robustly (strip all leading separators of both '/' and '\\' if the intention is to treat leading separators as classpath-style relative).
- Java version compatibility:
  - Arrays.stream(...).map(Path::toString).toList() uses Stream.toList(), which is only available in Java 16+. The code already uses Path.of (Java 11), so mixing APIs may cause compatibility problems. Use Collectors.toList() or Collectors.joining for safe compatibility with Java 11+:
    - e.g., Arrays.stream(candidates).map(Path::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "))
- Exception handling:
  - Throwing IllegalArgumentException for missing file is OK, but message construction currently appends a List object; using joining yields a clearer message.
  - Catching Exception around Files.readString is broad. Consider catching IOException specifically. Wrapping in IllegalStateException is acceptable but be explicit.
- Race conditions / security:
  - There is a potential TOCTOU/race where the file can change between existence check and read—common to most code using Files.exists then read. For most tools this is acceptable, but if security is a concern, mention it.
  - The method resolves candidates that may normalize to paths outside the project root (e.g., with "../"). If the intention is to limit to project directory, verify the resolved path is within an allowed root (e.g., resolved.startsWith(cwd) or the specific roots).
- Resource management:
  - Files.readString handles resources internally; no explicit resource leak concerns here.

4) Code quality (documentation, readability)
- No JavaDoc: Add class and method JavaDoc describing:
  - Purpose of the utility,
  - What kinds of path strings are accepted (leading slash treated as classpath-style, etc.),
  - Security constraints (if any),
  - Which roots are searched and in what order.
- Comments: There are helpful inline comments, but the behavior (treat leading slash as classpath-style) should be documented in the method JavaDoc for callers.
- Readability: Splitting the method into smaller methods will improve readability and make each behavior explicit.

5) Common anti-patterns
- Magic strings and numbers:
  - The hardcoded "src/main/java" and "src/test/java" are magic values. If these are meaningful project conventions, extract them as constants and document them.
  - The single "/" literal removal is a magic behavior—document it or make it configurable.
- Naive string handling:
  - Only removes the first leading '/', not multiple or backslashes, reducing portability.
- Deep nesting: Not an issue here; nesting is shallow.
- Use of stream.toList (possible API incompatibility), as noted above.

Concrete suggestions / example fixes
- Replace Spring dependency and blank check:
  - if (path == null || path.isBlank()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Path must not be blank");
  - remove import org.springframework.util.StringUtils;
- Add private constructor:
  - private FileUtils() { throw new AssertionError("Utility class"); }
- Split method into smaller helpers (example signatures):
  - private static String normalizeInput(String path)
  - private static Path[] buildCandidates(String normalized)
  - private static Path findExisting(Path[] candidates)
  - private static String readFileContent(Path resolved) throws IOException
- Improve candidate not found message and Java version safe joining:
  - String tried = Arrays.stream(candidates).map(Path::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
  - throw new IllegalArgumentException("File not found. Tried: " + tried);
- Better leading separator handling (example):
  - String normalized = trimmed.replaceFirst("^[\\\\/]+", "");
  - This removes all leading slashes/backslashes.
  - Document that absolute paths (Unix-style leading '/') are treated as classpath-style relative; this might be surprising to callers — consider offering another method or behavior toggle if absolute paths should be respected.
- Prevent escape outside project roots if desired:
  - After resolving and normalizing, check permitted roots:
    - if (!resolved.startsWith(cwd) && !resolved.startsWith(cwd.resolve("src/main/java")) && !resolved.startsWith(cwd.resolve("src/test/java"))) { reject } 
  - Alternatively, canonicalize and compare.
- Use Files.isRegularFile(p) directly (no need to call Files.exists before):
  - if (Files.isRegularFile(p)) { resolved = p; break; }
- Narrow exception catching when reading:
  - catch (IOException ex) { throw new IllegalStateException("Failed to read file: " + resolved, ex); }

Small code sketch illustrating many of the suggested changes (concise, not full):
- Add private constructor.
- Use isBlank instead of Spring.
- Remove single-leading-slash using regex.
- Use Collectors.joining for message.
- Use smaller helper methods.

Final checklist / action items
- [ ] Add JavaDoc to class and method describing behavior and search order.
- [ ] Remove Spring StringUtils dependency; use String.isBlank or Objects.requireNonNull + isBlank.
- [ ] Make utility class non-instantiable (private constructor).
- [ ] Split readFile into smaller methods for validation, normalization, candidate creation, resolution, and reading.
- [ ] Make leading-separator handling cross-platform and remove all leading slashes/backslashes if that is intended, or clearly document the behavior (or change to respect absolute paths).
- [ ] Replace Stream.toList() with a Java 11-compatible collector if you need to support Java 11.
- [ ] Consider restricting resolved paths to allowed roots if you want to prevent reading arbitrary files outside the project.

If you want, I can provide a refactored version of this class implementing the suggestions above (split methods, improved checks, JavaDoc, and no Spring dependency).
